Consequently, checkpoints regarding breeding plumage (green head/white ring) and male-specific tail feathers (curl) were correctly marked as absent. The bill color checkpoint was also correctly marked false as it lacks the specific drake coloration. The Router was not too lenient; in fact, it accurately flagged the gender mismatch which is the primary failure mode here.

alignment_reasoning: Severe alignment failure. The target class is 'drake' (male duck), but the image clearly shows a female mallard (brown mottled plumage, no green head, no curled tail). Only generic duck features (body shape, dark eyes, webbed feet structure) are present. The fine-grained classifier predicted 'drake' likely due to broad category overlap, but the visual evidence contradicts the specific taxonomic requirements of the label. 3/7 checkpoints passed (generic features), 4/7 failed (sex-specific features).
